content: Pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic studies, as well as pharmaceutical formulation studies, must be conducted to ensure the development of safe and effective medications specifically tailored for pediatric populations. It is essential to address the unique physiological and developmental characteristics of children to optimize drug efficacy and safety. Member States and funding organizations should actively support initiatives aimed at enhancing regulatory expertise in pediatric medicine. This includes fostering academic expertise and building capacity for conducting pediatric clinical trials, which are critical for generating robust evidence to guide therapeutic interventions in children. Clinical trials involving elderly and very elderly populations should be integrated into all stages of clinical development from the outset. These trials are necessary to address the specific health needs of these age groups, considering their unique pharmacological responses and comorbidities. Studies involving elderly and very elderly individuals should be conducted across diverse healthcare settings, including hospitals, community clinics, and remote areas, to ensure comprehensive data collection and applicability of findings. Pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic studies, along with pharmaceutical formulation research, are also crucial for developing safe and effective medications for elderly and very elderly populations. These studies should account for age-related physiological changes and polypharmacy considerations. Member States and funding bodies should support efforts to strengthen regulatory expertise in geriatric medicine. Additionally, academic institutions should be encouraged to develop the necessary expertise and infrastructure to conduct clinical trials in elderly populations, ensuring that this underrepresented group is adequately studied in medical research.
